Midnight on the Water

A common session tune in my neck of the woods, something soothing at the end of a session that everyone can enjoy.
I believe, though, that it is a work in copyright, although I don’t know who the composer is. Can someone check this out, please?

Trevor

Composer

According to the Waltz Book I, Luke Thomasson wrote it, but Benny Thomasson holds the copywright on it through the Winwood Music Company.

Re: Midnight On The Water

Played a lot in our local sessions. There is also a song by the same name, written by Ron Kavana, and recorded by The Watersons among others. The song tune is different, but Luke Thomasson’s tune is used as an instrumental break between verses, to good effect.

Re: Midnight On The Water

Benny has said in recordings that he recalled his father and uncle composing it one night in 1900 on their porch, Texas panhandle. Similar tune in a song collected by Lomax from Oklahoma called Old Paint may have been derived from repurposing the Thomason fiddle piece, the singer originated in the Texas panhandle around the same time.

Re: Midnight On The Water

After listening to this waltz for a bunch of years there is no doubt in my mind that it draws heavily on the old cowboy tune “ Goodbye Old Paint, I’ma Leaving Cheyenne”. This was a wrap-up tune for Saturday night dancehalls from Texas to Wyoming. Another common wrap up number was “ Irene, Good Night”.
